I feel the need to share my findings on the matter of following my own path. This could be classified as self help/actualization. But to me this is also a path to enlightenment (an end of suffering and a deep understanding of the world).

I would like to tell you about my life after high school. Don't worry, it's not unnecessarily depressing, just a bit. I remember leaving for college. My girlfriend (now wife) and I decided to go to schools in different states, 3k miles away. I distinctly remember how I felt as I watched her leave for the airport. It was the first time I felt alone. It was a month before I left for my school. I was extremely depressed. On top of feeling lonely, she decided to start drinking when she got to school. This is normal for most college students, but we had both decided to abstain in high school. For some reason, this was like a punch to the gut. My father was an alcoholic (among other things) and I looked down on pretty much anyone who drank in excess, and as a alcohol virgin, she went nuts her first year. I honestly am surprised we stayed together through this knowing who I was then, but we did.

When I arrived in school I settled in quite well. I waved my mother farewell and turned around with a new world at my feet. I had new material to learn, friends to make, a relationship to maintain, and a new city to get used to. Despite my other half not being there, I had a wonderful time. It felt good. Made some of the best friends I have. I graduated after 2 years and moved out to the desert so my girlfriend could finish her bachelors.

Again, I had a new environment. I had to get a full time job, start my career, and begin paying off my loans. I didn't realize it, but I was about to enter a long depression. My life until this point was planned out. School, then more school, then college, ??????, profit. I was excited to be an adult and get to make all my own decisions. But I realized in all my years I never learned to take charge and lead my own life. I worked, I paid rent, I payed my bills on time, but I didn't know where to go or what to do. So now I'm just supposed to work until I die, huh? It's a grim thought that most of us face, I feel.

The next 9 years were spent drifting. I didn't strive for more knowledge, or a promotion, or to advance my career, I had no aspirations. I had many opportunities to become a sous chef, but never took them. I didn't want to be taken advantage of once I was on a salary. I just wanted to work 40 hours, pay what I needed to pay, and play video games/fuck around on 4chan. Even in those tasks I didn't try. If something was challenging in a game, I tried to just get it over with asap or play games where exploration is the focus. On 4chan I started a small following with the evolution game, but I failed to dedicate to it or evolve the idea. I tried to invent my own wargame, but never finished it. I also began to invent my own fantasy world. I re-worked the framework almost every year and am just now really fleshing it out. But I'm no tolkein - it's something I brainstorm a lot, but rarely work on.

In short, I had no drive, I never challenged myself, and I was just another loser floating through this dreary and awful world. This, of course, didn't stop me from feeling superior to everyone I know.

My girlfriend and I moved back home and are now renting out my mom's house. I switched my career a few times, but all I wanted from a career was "not cooking". So naturally, I attracted a few jobs that got me nowhere, but at least showed me a life outside of cooking.

A few years ago I found Reddit. I stayed far away for a long time since everyone on 4chan talked about how shitty it is. Of course, 4chan talks about how shitty everything is. My life actually began to improve once I switched over to Reddit rather than 4chan. Now this is not an advertisement for modern Reddit, this was around 2013/2014. I wasn't aware of the censorship for a while, but I did find a few subreddits that were amazing. /personalfinance/, /gardening/, /writing/, /beermoney/, and the list goes on. I actually managed to crank out 50K words of a novel idea I had during NaNoWriMo (national novel writing month). I was gardening more, I was creating spreadsheets to track my financing, I was making huge improvements in my life and I felt really good. This was because I was surrounding myself with people with like-minded interests, but also because I was in a place that didn't treat everything as extremely negative. 4chan has always been nihilistic/pessimistic and reddit is unrealistically opportunistic. Both are huge traps, but exposing myself to this changed my consciousness and thus, my life.

Of course, I ended up leaving reddit and 4chan for a while once censorship ramped up and was made too obvious. But that year 2014 was the year my life really changed. It was also the year that my wife and I conceived our son.

I've been on a spiritual quest for a long time, and I still have a long way to go. But I feel that I am coming closer to what makes me happy, what gives me purpose, and what will allow me to live a long and full life. So that's why I started this series of posts. I want to share how I feel and what can help others on Voat.

I left out some details, but if you have any questions please let me know. I love you guys and gals.
